name: color-gamut
plain: Widest color space the screen shows: sRGB, P3 or Rec2020.
meaning: P3 separates Apple devices and OLED phones from budget screens. A few bits of hardware signal.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can check whether your screen shows standard, wide P3 or very wide Rec2020 colors
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads.
can: Ask whether your screen supports P3 or Rec2020
Serve richer images and colors if it does
Add the answer to a browser fingerprint
cannot: See your exact color profile or calibration
limits.reach_label: One yes or no, no prompt

story.what_it_is: Asks whether your screen can show a wide range of colors, such as the P3 range.

marketing.name: High definition CSS color guide
marketing.pitch: Teaches developers how to use wide gamut color on newer screens and fall back safely on older ones.

marketing.name: color-gamut media feature
marketing.pitch: Documents a media query that tells a page which range of colors the screen can show.

story.for_you: You never get asked. If your screen is wide gamut, a site can show richer reds and greens. If not, it quietly uses safer colors.
story.for_makers: Brands want their exact orange or green to look right. Developers use the check to switch to wide colors only where they will show. It also adds a small clue to device profiles.

use_cases.example: A fashion or paint store shows richer swatches on a P3 screen so a red sofa looks closer to real life.
A photo editor in the browser warns when your screen cannot show all the colors in an image.
A WebGL game turns on a more vivid look for sunsets and neon on screens that can show it.
A streaming site offers wider color video only to screens that can really show it.
A brand ad uses the exact brand color in wide gamut on newer phones and laptops.
A fingerprint script notes the gamut as one more clue to group devices.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
